findings.summary: The plan does not weigh the risk that the replay holds the job when more past readings are newly refused than the declared share allows.
findings.evidence: replay_limit_percent gives declared + REPLAY_DECLARED_MARGIN_POINTS (5). With the reading's 3% the limit is 8%. Every stored accepted reading that has a free-form `question` will now be refused by check_reading_text. The snapshot has no records, so that share cannot be read here. The plan calls 3% an estimate and says 'the replay at verification measures the real share'. It never says what the producer does if the in-loop replay (run/mod.rs:2368-2373) reports more than 8%. Fix: Add a risk: if the in-loop replay goes over the limit, the producer reports the measured share and the newly refused readings as a finding for Athena or the customer. It must not narrow the rule to grandfather old readings or edit the declared share.
findings.location: Risks / Dependents entry 'Replay hold on the newly refused share' (crates/athena-core/src/reading/replay.rs:13,161,304)

findings.summary: The accepted form is described two ways, so the parser and its tests could disagree.
findings.evidence: The approach says the question 'must end with `Default: (x)`'. Step 2 only requires that some label token in the text after the last `default:` matches an alternative. That accepts `Default: (a) because it is shorter.` and `Default: (z) or (a)`. Fix: Pick one rule and pin it with a corpus case. For example: the first label token after the last `Default:` must be one of the alternatives' labels, and trailing explanation is allowed. Word the approach, the doc comment and the refusal text the same way.
findings.location: Approach ('must end with `Default: (x)`') vs Step 2 (split at the last `default:` and require a label token in the tail)

findings.summary: reading.rs has its own list of child-module sources, and the plan leaves it as is.
findings.evidence: refusal_corpus.rs and reading.rs each keep an include_str! list of reading child modules. Step 8 adds questions.rs only to the corpus list. Nothing in the plan's reading.rs tests searches that source for check_reader_question, so nothing breaks today, but the two lists drift apart. Fix: Also add include_str!("reading/questions.rs") to the reading.rs test-module reading_source(), before reading.rs.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot, reading the code only. The main claims hold. refusing_check (checks.rs:518) is the only place the gate runs reading checks. read_for calls check_reading_acceptance right after build_reading (reading.rs:659-689). check_reading_text reaches the same checks from the steward (steward.rs:421) and from `athena check-reading` (main.rs:678). The reader token budget counts only CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults and catalog (lib.rs:284-285), so the new READING_RULES line sits outside it. has_addressee and says_code_answers are private in admission.rs (lines 551, 559) and can be widened as described. The briefs test (briefs.rs:3470-3536) asserts 11 rules and a section under 3150 bytes, which the plan updates. Wiring the rule as the first step in refusing_check instead of inside build_reading is a sound, well-argued reading of criterion 1: putting it inside build_reading would bypass the replay and break the corpus rules. The plan explains why it touches checks.rs and the two briefs files (Athena's three minor scope findings); none of them is a governance file. Each demonstration runs the real gate with no test doubles, and each would fail without the behaviour. The label parser is deterministic and does not count `file(s)`-style words as alternatives. The dependents list matches the callers I found by searching for check_reading_text. What is left is minor: the plan should say what happens if the replay finds more than 8% of past readings newly refused, and the "Default:" form is described two ways. Neither stops the plan, so I accept it.
